findings.title: Data race on shared err and counter in concurrent index build loop
findings.body: In searchSupport.init, every goroutine spawned via group.Go writes to the outer err variable (`_, _, err = s.build(ctx, ...)`) and increments totalBatchesIndexed without any synchronization. With initWorkers > 1 (the whole point of this PR is concurrent namespace builds), these are concurrent reads/writes of shared variables: a Go data race that will fail under -race, the trace event count (span.AddEvent using totalBatchesIndexed) can be wrong, and worse, the closure returns the shared err — if goroutine A's build fails but goroutine B overwrites err with nil before A's `return err` is evaluated, errgroup sees nil and startup succeeds with a failed/missing index. Use a local variable inside the closure (`_, _, berr := s.build(...); return berr`) and an atomic counter (or compute the count from len(stats)).

findings.title: Watch goroutine panics on closed events channel and uses a never-canceled context
findings.body: The watch loop started at the end of searchSupport.init uses `watchctx := context.Background()` (so it is never canceled on server shutdown) and then does `for { v := <-events; s.handleEvent(watchctx, v) }` without checking the receive's ok flag. The SQL backend's poller closes the events channel when the backend stops; receiving from a closed channel returns nil immediately, so handleEvent dereferences a nil *WrittenEvent at `evt.Type` — an unrecovered panic in this goroutine crashes the entire process during shutdown (and absent the panic the loop would spin at 100% CPU). Because this PR makes init run unconditionally at server construction, this goroutine now always starts. It should be `v, ok := <-events; if !ok { return }`, and the context should be tied to the server lifecycle. Note the same unguarded-receive pattern exists in initWatcher in server.go.

findings.title: No guard against concurrent BuildIndex for the same key after removing the whole-function lock
findings.body: BuildIndex now only locks cacheMu for the final cache insert, and nothing prevents two goroutines from building the same NamespacedResource concurrently: searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex checks GetIndex and then builds outside any lock (its own TODO acknowledges this), so two simultaneous Search requests, or a watch event racing a search, for a namespace that was skipped at startup (below InitMinCount) or newly created will both call BuildIndex. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) both call bleve.New on the same directory, so one fails with a store-lock/already-exists error that is surfaced to the user even though nothing is actually wrong; for in-memory indexes one fully built index is silently discarded by the last cache write and IndexTenants is double-counted. The previous whole-function mutex at least serialized these duplicate builds. A per-key lock or singleflight around check-build-cache would fix it.

findings.title: No test coverage for the new eager-init contract
findings.body: NewResourceServer now runs s.Init synchronously and returns an error when backend init or the index build fails, and the s.Init(ctx) guards were removed from every gRPC handler (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, IsHealthy, PutBlob, GetBlob) — but no test was added or updated to cover the new contract: that construction-time init failures propagate, or that handlers behave correctly without ever calling Init. The only test change in the PR skips the postgres variant of the one integration test that exercises the storage-server target. A unit test around NewResourceServer init success/failure (e.g., with a failing StorageBackend) would catch regressions in this new startup behavior.
